decision_contract.target: Choose evidence collection for a reported CVE on an asset, not discover a new weakness or assign VEX status.
decision_contract.source: Implementation-level claims require source evidence under the project policy; this does not guarantee the current analyzer can prove them.
decision_contract.operator: Operator-observable deployed settings/records can select operational review, but operator reports cannot prove code absence or exploitability.
decision_contract.specialist: Hardware, model robustness, cryptographic design, covert channels and design/documentation claims require additional artifacts; do not silently send them to a software parser.
decision_contract.baseline_vs_case: The CWE record defines a baseline. Explicit CVE implementation/configuration mechanisms can refine it before the workflow starts.
decision_contract.mapping: Official Prohibited/Discouraged CVE mappings defer for a better mapping. Allowed-with-Review remains visibly flagged.
decision_contract.availability: Source availability selects workflow 1/2/3 only after the evidence requirement is determined. It never determines that requirement.
decision_contract.verdict: Every route starts under investigation. Routing, matching quotes and complete taxonomy coverage never authorize not_affected or affected.

memory_bounds_lifetime.label: Bounds, object lifetime and affected operations

input_to_sensitive_operation.label: Input validation, normalization and input-to-operation data flow

authorization_enforcement.label: Authorization/authentication checks on every affected code path

state_control_flow.label: Control flow, synchronization, state transitions and ordering

reference_resolution.label: Name, path, object and resource-reference resolution

calculation_semantics.label: Arithmetic, comparison, types and encoding semantics

crypto_implementation.label: Cryptographic validation, key handling and randomness implementation

communication_configuration.label: Actual communication path, encryption and enabled protocol configuration

resource_permissions.label: Effective resource ownership, permissions and access-control records

account_policy.label: Configured accounts, password policy and credential lifecycle records

key_configuration.label: Vendor key/certificate replacement or rotation records, without secret key material

feature_configuration.label: Vendor-documented feature and deployment configuration records

actor_and_access_scope.label: Actual actors, roles, accessible interfaces and operating scope

hardware_design.label: RTL, circuit/register design, hardware specification or physical measurement

design_documentation.label: Design, architecture, lifecycle or technical documentation

model_robustness_evaluation.label: Model/data artifacts and adversarial robustness evaluation

side_channel_measurement.label: Information-flow threat model and timing/storage/physical measurements

cryptographic_design_review.label: Cryptographic primitive/design assurance and implementation test evidence

cve_specific_mechanism.label: More specific CVE/vendor mechanism evidence before selecting a method

rules.rationale: Memory/index/lifetime claims require implementation-level definitions and operation evidence.
Validation/neutralization cannot be established by a configured-service answer alone.
Verify implementation checks and the deployed actor/role/interface scope separately.
Resource state, event ordering and control-flow claims require implementation paths.
Resource/reference interpretation depends on implementation resolution, not names alone.
Arithmetic/type/comparison correctness requires operation and input semantics.
Missing or incorrect error handling requires inspection of handling paths.
Validation, embedded credentials, negotiation and random generation need implementation evidence plus deployment scope.
A reported enabled control does not establish enforcement on all relevant paths.
This weakness describes implementation structure or behavior requiring source/definition evidence.
Review documented transport behavior against actual protocol/path records. This does not prove absence of implementation defects.
A weak algorithm may be embedded in code or selected by deployment configuration. Require CVE/vendor mechanism evidence before choosing the method.
Hash construction, padding and password-hash work parameters require implementation/parameter evidence unless an explicit observable vendor configuration mechanism is established.
A primitive with a risky implementation needs design/implementation assurance; an enabled-cipher answer is insufficient.
Public/private/final declarations are source-language properties, not deployed filesystem/account permissions.
Effective permissions and account/process privileges are operator-observable with records.
Inspect effective account/password/lifecycle settings without treating a report as code proof.
Review vendor-supported key replacement/rotation records. An explicit embedded/hard-coded key mechanism adds a source requirement.
Documented cookie and transport settings can be inspected in deployed service records.
Deployment/exposure settings are observable; reports remain non-authoritative for final negative VEX decisions.
Software source or operator answers alone do not establish design/lifecycle/documentation properties.
The specific weakness requires hardware/register/processor/physical evidence beyond the software source analyzers.
Verify state representation/synchronization and the actual participating components; hardware-specific metadata still requires specialist evidence.
Adversarial model behavior needs model/data robustness evaluation; ordinary source parsing is insufficient.
Timing/storage channels need a threat model and information-flow/measurement evidence, not only a missing call path.
Resource emergence or security-identity/key-design assumptions need explicit design evidence.
Distinguish implemented token generation from configurable deployed credential expiration using CVE/vendor evidence.
The broad weakness includes both implementation and deployment mechanisms; obtain CVE-specific evidence.

specialist_definition_pattern: (?i)\b(?:hardware|on-chip|semiconductor|circuit|registers?|lock bit|fuse values|fabric bridge|processor instructions|electromagnetic|power save|physical access control|microarchitectur[a-z]*|transient execution)\b

operational_refinements.pattern: (?i)(?:\b(?:misconfiguration|configuration file|configuration option|server setting|access policy)\b|\.htaccess\b).{0,60}\b(?:authorization|authentication|access control)|\b(?:authorization|authentication|access control)\b.{0,60}(?:\b(?:misconfiguration|configuration file|configuration option|server setting|access policy|disabled by default)\b|\.htaccess\b)
